title: Streaming comes to API Gateway: real-time and AI-ready APIs, without changing your spec
desc: API Gateway now supports real-time streaming—including Server-Sent Events, WebSockets, gRPC, and chunked transfer encoding—in Public Preview without requiring changes to your existing API specifications. This update allows developers to route long-lived, bi-directional streams and AI workloads directly through the gateway while maintaining consistent authentication, rate limiting, and observability. Additionally, gateways now feature deterministic default hostnames, simplifying environment provisioning and infrastructure-as-code management.
author: Google for Developers

title: Architecting Governed, Self-Evolving AI Agents on Google Cloud
desc: Learn how Project Chrysalis combines Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agent Development Kit (ADK), BigQuery, and a four-gate defense-in-depth security stack (Model Armor, Cloud KMS, Binary Authorization, and OPA) to build governed, self-evolving AI agents that remediate live production outages in 1.8 seconds.
author: Google for Developers

title: Powering the Agent Development Lifecycle with any framework, from ADK to LangChain and beyond
desc: The Agents CLI Extension System enables developers to use frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or custom enterprise stacks while retaining a unified deployment and evaluation workflow. It details a first-party LangChain template that scaffolds, runs, and deploys agents without requiring the Agent Development Kit (ADK). Additionally, it demonstrates how platform teams can author custom extensions to enforce policies such as automated software bill of materials (SBOM) scans during deployment.
author: Google for Developers

title: Announcing New vLLM and SGLang Inference Engines on TPU
desc: This post announces native PyTorch backends for vLLM and SGLang powered by TorchTPU, enabling developers to run and optimize serving workloads using familiar PyTorch tools. Built in collaboration with open-source project maintainers, these engines include optimized TPU kernel implementations, production-ready features like KV cache management with TPU Sync, and disaggregated serving. Public benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and industry-leading cost efficiency on Ironwood TPU across long-context and agentic workloads.
author: Google for Developers

title: Bringing Visual Graph Debugging to Custom Edge Compilers with Model Explorer
desc: Google AI Edge Model Explorer now supports custom compiler intermediate representations and open-source adapters like TOSA, VGF, and PTE for on-device machine learning. Developers can leverage hierarchical graph visualization, split-pane views, and per-node trace overlays to catch export regressions and verify hardware delegation. These tools enable engineering teams to transparently debug execution graphs and pinpoint cycle-level latency bottlenecks locally.
author: Google for Developers

title: Unifying Edge AI: How Coral NPU’s open standard brings portable, energy-viable intelligence from model to silicon
desc: Google Research has completed the 32-bit open-source Coral NPU RISC-V architecture with the introduction of its Matrix Execution Unit, which delivers up to 1 TOPS while targeting 10 mW average power for edge inference. Alongside this architecture, the release of the v1.0 open-source IREE/MLIR compiler allows developers to take models from JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow straight to Coral NPU hardware without writing custom assembly. Developers can now prototype and deploy these multimodal edge applications using new hardware options like the Synaptics Astra SR200 MCU series and globally available Coralboard devkits.12
author: Google for Developers

title: Integrating TorchTPU into TorchTitan and Optimizing Models for TPU
desc: TorchTPU integrates a native torch.device("tpu") backend directly into PyTorch, allowing developers to train large-scale models on Google Cloud TPUs without rewriting code in JAX. The TorchTitan TPU fork enhances this with production-grade scaling primitives like SimpleFSDP, Graph Trainer, and custom Pallas kernels that achieve high Model Flops Utilization (MFU) across dense and MoE architectures. Developers can leverage these battle-tested optimization playbooks, recipes, and the Hugging Face modeling backend to efficiently scale their own workloads on TPU infrastructure.
author: Google for Developers

title: Native Model Authoring for Edge with LiteRT Tensor API
desc: Meet the LiteRT Tensor API: giving developers native C++ control over the model graph to unify end-to-end ML computations on heterogeneous edge hardware.
author: Google for Developers

title: Step by Step guide: Build a Voice Agent That Never Goes Silent using ADK
desc: The open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK) and gemini-3.8-live enable developers to build responsive voice agents by implementing non-blocking tools in Python. Developers can use streaming tools to yield progress updates or background execution patterns to keep conversations fluid during long-running backend queries. Additionally, configuring response scheduling behaviors such as WHEN_IDLE, INTERRUPT, or SILENT gives developers precise control over when and how tool results are delivered into the conversation.
author: Google for Developers

title: Announcing DPoP Support for Google OAuth: Securing Refresh Tokens
desc: Google OAuth Platform now supports DPoP (Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession) to sender-constrain refresh tokens, neutralizing Infostealer malware and adversary-in-the-middle attacks. By cryptographically binding long-lived refresh tokens while maintaining short-lived access tokens as standard Bearer tokens, developers achieve robust credential security without incurring high-QPS API performance overhead. Additionally, developers integrating multi-agent or Model Context Protocol (MCP) workloads can use Google Cloud Secure Token Service (STS) to handle secure token delegation across agent chains.
author: Google for Developers

title: Evaluating AI agents: moving past the vibe check
desc: A practical engineering guide and reference architecture for establishing continuous evaluation pipelines for multi-turn AI agents using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Google ADK, and OpenInference standards.
author: Google for Developers

title: Three layers, one repo: a tour of google/adk-recipes
desc: The google/adk-recipes repository unifies Agent Development Kit (ADK) resources into three structured layers—core/, plugins/, and contrib/—serving as a single source of truth for building AI agents. Developers can leverage reference patterns, install modular vertical skills (such as retail product search and virtual try-on) directly into their coding assistants, and deploy production-ready services across multiple languages. This cohesive structure streamlines the entire workflow from initial scaffolding to full deployment on Google Cloud infrastructure.
author: Google for Developers

title: Announcing MCP support in Apigee hybrid: agentic tools that run in your own cluster
desc: Apigee hybrid 1.17.0 introduces native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, enabling the MCP data plane to run directly within your own Kubernetes cluster. This architecture ensures that AI agent request traffic and tool execution remain entirely inside your infrastructure while pulling configuration updates from the control plane. Developers can expose OpenAPI 3.0.x specifications as discoverable MCP tools, leverage existing security policies and API products, and trace end-to-end requests using W3C trace context headers.
author: Google for Developers

title: Optimizing a 200,000-line Python codebase overnight with Gemini 4 Argon
desc: How our engineering team ran Gemini 4 Argon unattended overnight with .agents/skills and /goal mode to cut in-memory session prep overhead by 40% in long sessions and speed up cold imports by 21% in Google's open-source Python Agent Development Kit (ADK).
author: Google for Developers

title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
desc: Gemini 4 Argon is a general-purpose physical reasoning model designed to enhance workflows across the robotics stack with advanced capabilities in physical understanding, code generation, and visual-semantic reasoning. Developers can access and integrate Argon across Google's developer platforms—including Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, and Google Antigravity—to build and test sophisticated robotic applications. By leveraging simulation tools like MuJoCo and code-as-policies, engineers can seamlessly transition from real-world data or sketches to physically verified robot control and self-improvement workflows.
author: Google for Developers

title: ML Drift: Next-Gen GPU AI/ML Inference at the Edge
desc: Google AI Edge has introduced ML Drift, a high-performance, universal GPU compute framework designed to accelerate on-device AI and machine learning inference. By abstracting the complexities of hardware and low-level APIs—including OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU—ML Drift enables developers to build real-time, interactive ML experiences, from sophisticated video effects to generative AI, across mobile and desktop platforms.
author: Google for Developers

title: The Outer Loop, Insights First: An Ambient Quality Agent That Diagnoses Your Production Agent
desc: How do you keep improving an AI agent after the first 80%, once it serves real production traffic and silent quality regressions return HTTP 200 OK? We are open-sourcing AQuA (Ambient Quality Agent), a reference implementation that runs beside your production agent in Google Cloud, sweeps and verifies failure clusters against conversation transcripts, and diagnoses root causes anchored to the exact deployed source snapshot.
author: Google for Developers

title: Supercharge your development with the Google Developer Knowledge API ecosystem
desc: Google is launching the Developer Knowledge API and MCP Server in public preview. This new toolset provides a canonical, machine-readable way for AI assistants and agentic platforms to search and retrieve up-to-date documentation across Firebase, Google Cloud, Android, and more. By using the official MCP server, developers can connect tools directly to Google’s documentation corpus, ensuring that AI-generated code and guidance are based on authoritative, real-time context.
author: Google for Developers

title: EmbeddingGemma 2: The Developer Guide
desc: EmbeddingGemma 2 is a compact, open-source multimodal embedding model that maps text, code, images, video, and audio into a unified 768-dimensional space. Developers can use the sentence-transformers library to selectively load modular modality encoders—ranging from 270M to 740M parameters—to optimize memory usage. Additionally, Matryoshka Representation Learning enables dynamic dimension truncation down to 128d, significantly reducing vector database storage requirements while maintaining high retrieval performance.
author: Google for Developers

title: Bring multimodal semantic search to the edge with EmbeddingGemma 2
desc: EmbeddingGemma 2 is a new 740M open-weight multimodal model that maps text, images, video, and audio into a unified vector space for privacy-first, on-device retrieval. Developers can easily integrate these capabilities cross-platform using MediaPipe Tasks or optimize fine-grained performance across CPU, GPU, and NPU accelerators with LiteRT. The model enables ultra-low-latency local solutions like search-as-you-type media retrieval, keyframe video moments finding, and zero-shot intent routing.
author: Google for Developers
